decisions.reason: Changing the default document language to English does not alter which style system must be implemented or its required coverage.
The accepted proposal explicitly distinguishes an English document default from Danish style names, and the existing same-message MODIFY already records the Danish style-name language.
The document default-language change does not alter the required stability of copying legacy NXQ content into the new templates.
Table and column containment after pasting is independent of the template's default document language.
Reliable manual line breaks after legacy-content pasting remain required regardless of the default document language.
Tab-driven sublevel creation and list alignment behavior are unaffected by the default document language.
The supported Word for Windows environment and reliability expectations remain unchanged when the document default becomes English.
Bullet sizing, alignment, balance, and scaling requirements are independent of the default document language.
